pharm: Topical fluoroquinolone that inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, active against Cutibacterium (Propionibacterium) acnes and Staphylococcus species; also has anti-inflammatory activity
quick: Apply a thin layer of 1% cream/lotion to affected skin twice daily
Limited data; use only if clearly needed (avoid extensive use)
Limited data; avoid application to the breast; use cautiously
summary: Nadifloxacin is a topical fluoroquinolone antibacterial used for acne vulgaris and superficial bacterial skin infections in many countries (Europe, Japan, India and elsewhere). Applied as a 1% cream or lotion twice daily, it inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV and is active against Cutibacterium acnes and staphylococci, with additional anti-inflammatory effects. Systemic absorption is minimal, so it is generally well tolerated with mainly local reactions (dryness, irritation, contact dermatitis). It is NOT FDA-approved; information here is based on EMA/SmPC and manufacturer prescribing data. It is for external use only, avoiding eyes and mucous membranes.
indications: Superficial bacterial skin infections caused by susceptible organisms (e.g. folliculitis, impetigo) per local labeling

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer of 1% cream or lotion to the affected area twice daily (morning and evening)
dosage.n: Continue for several weeks; review at ~8-12 weeks

dosage.d: Apply 1% cream thinly to the affected area twice daily

admin: Wash and dry the affected skin, then apply a thin layer to the area twice daily
For external cutaneous use only - avoid contact with the eyes, lips and other mucous membranes
Wash hands after application; do not apply to broken or heavily weeping skin unless directed
Avoid prolonged or widespread use to limit the risk of bacterial resistance
moa: Nadifloxacin is a fluoroquinolone that inhibits the bacterial enzymes DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, blocking bacterial DNA replication and transcription and producing bactericidal activity against Cutibacterium acnes and Staphylococcus species. It also exerts anti-inflammatory effects relevant to acne.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to nadifloxacin, other quinolones or any formulation excipient
relative: Application to large body-surface areas or under occlusion (limits resistance/absorption)
Use on mucous membranes or near the eyes

preg: There are limited data on topical nadifloxacin in pregnancy. Systemic exposure is minimal, but use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and avoid widespread or prolonged application. (Not FDA-approved; based on EMA/SmPC guidance.)
lact: It is not known whether nadifloxacin is excreted in human milk; systemic absorption is low. Avoid applying to the breast area in breastfeeding women and use cautiously elsewhere.
renal: No dose adjustment is required because systemic absorption from topical use is minimal.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required because systemic absorption from topical use is minimal.

minor: Other topical irritants/peeling agents (benzoyl peroxide, retinoids, alcohol-based products) - additive local irritation if applied to the same area at the same time
interactions.alcohol: Not applicable (topical); avoid applying alcohol-based products simultaneously to reduce irritation
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically significant laboratory interference (minimal systemic absorption)

emergency: Signs of a severe allergic reaction (widespread rash, facial swelling, difficulty breathing) - rare with topical use

monitoring: Clinical response of acne or skin infection over several weeks
counsel: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin twice daily after gently cleansing and drying the area
For external use only - keep away from the eyes, lips and inside of the nose/mouth; wash hands after applying
Mild dryness, redness or stinging may occur; if severe irritation develops, stop and contact your doctor
Do not use other strong topical products on the same area at the same time unless advised
Improvement in acne may take several weeks - use regularly and as directed
Avoid prolonged unnecessary use to help prevent bacterial resistance
pk: Local antibacterial/anti-inflammatory action at the application site
Minimal systemic absorption; high local skin concentrations
Systemic half-life not clinically relevant given low absorption
Store at room temperature, protect from heat; keep the cap closed and out of reach of children
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - marketed in Europe, Japan, India and elsewhere; information here is from EMA/SmPC and manufacturer data rather than openFDA
Topical fluoroquinolone for acne/superficial skin infection - active against C. acnes and staphylococci with added anti-inflammatory effect
Minimal systemic absorption, so no renal/hepatic dose adjustment and mainly local side effects
Limit duration/area of use to reduce the risk of selecting fluoroquinolone-resistant skin flora; external use only
missed: If an application is missed, apply it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next application, in which case skip it. Do not apply a double amount to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Topical overdose (excessive application) is unlikely to cause systemic effects but may increase local irritation; remove excess product and treat irritation symptomatically. If accidentally ingested, provide supportive care and contact a poison control center.
